synoptic.summary: High pressure centred near the Utah/Colorado border keeps Thursday dry with light flow and persistent valley inversions, so the normal diurnal cycle runs: drainage from ~180° at POM in the morning, switch to flow from ~340°–350° around 11:00–14:00. Friday the flow aloft increases and mixes the inversions out; the launch forecasts then stay from 150°–190° all day with no afternoon switch — a departure from the usual pattern ahead of the next system. A weak Pacific Northwest trough brushes northern Utah Friday night into early Saturday (light valley rain, mainly north of I-80; 39–52% precipitation chance at the launches Saturday morning), followed by gusty post-frontal flow from 300°–330° Saturday — the Steep Mountain rotor direction for POM North. Winds aloft (GFS) failed to download this run, so rotor and mixing checks rely on the NWS transport wind and are less certain.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: With flow staying light, valley inversions will persist, resulting in some reduction in air quality. Flow aloft is on track to increase for Friday, allowing valley inversions to mix out and temperatures to trend upward, running 5-10F above seasonal normals.

pressure.significance: 1027.3 mb at Salt Lake airport (KSLC) at 19:54 Wed, up 0.7 mb in 24 h (1026.6 → 1027.3) with the usual evening rise of ~1.8 mb since 15:54. A steady high: light gradient Thursday, weakening as the trough approaches late Friday.

observations.summary: Evening observations (19:35–20:00 Wed), ~11 h before the Thursday morning slot — they say little about the morning. Salt Lake airport and South Valley Regional report light flow from 300° (4 kt); Spanish Fork (8°, 12 G15 kt) and Alpine (5°, 9 G11 kt) show a brisk evening canyon/down-valley flow from ~360°, while Lehi has already turned to 129° at 9 G11 kt — drainage starting near the gap, matching the forecast turn to 140°–160° tonight. Point of the Mountain station and Draper returned no observations. South Valley Regional's newest report is 01:35Z (1 h 44 min before this run) — older than the rest but not stale.
